scope: production crate in-process Release compute; independent fresh order runs on one Apple Metal device. No camera-native 4K source or view presentation timing.
clock: wall milliseconds from Instant; update/submit/queue completion and staging/host copies have separate endpoints
statistics: nearest-rank p50/p95; state alternates, pixels compared after each timed interval; all raw samples in acquisition order
memory: explicit buffer sizes; driver allocations, C++ references and host copies excluded

native.sampling: full original top-left pixel grid; JPEG is tagged sRGB; inverse sRGB EOTF, alpha 1; mask grey/255

4k.sampling: 3840x2160 nearest-neighbor expansion of original top-left crop (0,83,1600,983), identical pixel-center mapping for image and mask; JPEG is tagged sRGB; inverse sRGB EOTF, alpha 1; mask grey/255

timingBoundaries.residentParameterWriteCPU: host scheduling of a 304-byte parameter update, no waiting
timingBoundaries.residentUpdateSubmitComplete: parameter update, compute encoding, submit and completion fence; p50 gate uses this series
timingBoundaries.readbackAfterCompletion: new staging, output copy, map, host Vec and finite check after compute completion
timingBoundaries.residentUpdateThroughReadback: duration from update through explicit compute fence and full staging readback
timingBoundaries.freshBindUploadRenderReadback: validated host frame; fresh buffer allocation, image/mask upload, dispatch, tiling, readback and finite scan, with compiled plan and verified LUT already available

reproduce: python3 Modules/ImageEdit/tests/replay_mask.py prepare <frames> --full-frame  # native photographed frame

laterTextureIntegration.scope: The performance runs use the production buffer path. The later Metal IOSurface option shares the point operators and DAG generator. Its transport parity is measured separately; this receipt makes no IOSurface or window-latency claim.
